title: reference_verification weight claim is inverted: it was cut 0.20→0.15, and 'most critical predictor' refers to rental_history
evidence: architecture.md: "`reference_verification` is a first-class scoring category; weight raised 0.15 → 0.20 per `tenant_scorer/tools/scoring_tools.py` comment ("most critical predictor")." — Actual RightTenantryAgents/tenant_scorer/tools/scoring_tools.py: "# Rebalanced 2026-05-04 ... rental_history raised 0.15 -> 0.20 ("most critical predictor"); reference_verification, red_flag_detection, application_completeness reduced." and "WEIGHT_REFERENCE_VERIFICATION = 0.15  # Social proof of tenancy reliability". Git commit c86ff08 (2026-05-04): "-WEIGHT_REFERENCE_VERIFICATION = 0.20" → "+WEIGHT_REFERENCE_VERIFICATION = 0.15".
detail: The doc claims codebase verification on 2026-07-21 but inverts the May 2026 rebalance: reference_verification now weights 0.15 (reduced), and rental_history holds 0.20 and the 'most critical predictor' label. Overstates how much call evidence would move the score.
recommended_fix: Correct to 'reference_verification (weight 0.15) already exists; rental_history is the 0.20 most-critical-predictor category' in architecture.md and main report lines 331/398.

title: Proposed `reference_calling` consent type cites the `consent_record` pattern, which was deliberately renamed to `acknowledgement_record`
evidence: Main report: "a `consent_record` + `consent_type` pattern exists for the applicant-side attestation". Actual supabase/migrations/20260422000001_rename_consent_to_acknowledgement.sql: "ALTER TABLE consent_record RENAME TO acknowledgement_record;" with header "Renaming prevents future readers inferring a legal story that the code and privacy policy both refute." Current code: server/src/application/sql/create_acknowledgement_record.sql: "INSERT INTO acknowledgement_record (application_id, record_type, policy_version)".
detail: The 'verified current state' architecture thread anchors its applicant-attestation design on a table renamed three months earlier specifically to avoid implying consent as lawful basis — the same legal-story distinction the research's own legal thread (Art 6(1)(f)) depends on.
recommended_fix: Reference the `acknowledgement_record`/`record_type` pattern (enum type still named `consent_type`); note the rename rationale aligns with the report's legitimate-interest recommendation.

title: Report claims RightTenantry 'charges EUR 99/vacancy for AI analysis' — the AI-analysis unlock is €299; €99 is a 14-day vacancy extension
evidence: Main report: "RightTenantry already charges EUR 99/vacancy for AI analysis." Actual server/src/payment/payment_sku.gleam: "`VacancyUnlock` — one-off €299 unlock for unlimited AI analysis on a vacancy." / "`VacancyExtension` — €99 / +14 days extension of an active or recently-closed vacancy." CLAUDE.md: "EUR 299 per vacancy unlocks unlimited AI analysis."
detail: The viability economics anchor the per-vacancy margin argument ('margin impact ≈ nil at EUR 99; ~91% gross stands') on the wrong SKU. Conclusion only strengthens at €299, but the product fact is wrong in a codebase-grounded document.
recommended_fix: Replace 'EUR 99/vacancy' with the €299 VacancyUnlock price and re-state the margin line; distinguish the €99 extension SKU if mentioned.
